subject_entity.notes: Gnostic teacher; studied in Alexandria, later prominent in Rome c. 138–160. Founded Valentinianism, the most influential Gnostic school, teaching a complex pleroma of divine emanations (Aeons) and a demiurge subordinate to the supreme God. Opposed apostolic succession, bodily resurrection, and the authority of the OT.

object_entity.proposition_label: Faith is transmitted through apostolic succession
object_entity.description: The bishops who succeed the apostles are authoritative guarantors of the received tradition.

evidence.notes: Valentinus claimed private secret knowledge transmitted from Theudas (disciple of Paul) — bypassing apostolic succession.

passage.excerpt: Valentinus adapted the principles of the heretical school called Gnostic to his own peculiar character of school. He affirmed that in the invisible and ineffable heights there exists a perfect, pre-existent Aeon — Proarche, Propator, and Bythus — invisible and incomprehensible. With him was also Ennoia, whom he calls Charis and Sige. This Bythus, at last resolving to send forth from himself the beginning of all things, deposited this production as a seed in the womb of Sige. The result was Nous and Aletheia — the beginning of a vast pleroma of divine emanations.

object_entity.notes: Major Egyptian port city; intellectual and commercial center; seat of the Catechetical School; major Christian center from the first century onward.

evidence.notes: Clement reports Valentinus was educated in Alexandria before his Roman period.

passage.excerpt: Valentinus came to Rome in the time of Hyginus, flourished under Pius, and remained until Anicetus. Cerdo, his predecessor in heresy, had also established himself at Rome under Hyginus. Hegesippus records that Valentinus, Marcion, and others who taught contrary to the truth were active in Rome during this period, each founding a distinct school. Valentinus claimed to have received secret knowledge from Theudas, a disciple of Paul, through which he constructed his elaborate system of divine Aeons.

object_entity.proposition_label: Faith is transmitted through apostolic succession
object_entity.description: The bishops who succeed the apostles are authoritative guarantors of the received tradition.

evidence.notes: Marcion rejected the apostolic churches and their tradition, forming his own canon and hierarchy.

passage.excerpt: Marcion of Pontus succeeded [Cerdo] and developed his doctrine, blaspheming with shameless effrontery Him proclaimed as God by the law and the prophets, declaring Him the author of evils, taking delight in war, infirm of purpose, and contrary to Himself. But Jesus, derived from that father above the God who made the world, came into Judaea in the times of Pontius Pilate, was manifested in the form of a man — abolishing the prophets and the law — but not truly taking flesh. He also mutilated the Gospel according to Luke, removing all that is written respecting the generation of the Lord.
